note: Design (read 11-18, E5's first item, with P-052 and N-1067): a stage's pipelines are made while it loads, and a draw never compiles. (1) Pipelines are registered as the stage's materials register (registries_, game thread, during the load); the render thread queues the new ones each frame (render_core.cpp, pipelines_queued_) for low-priority workers. The game's load already ends at one gate, GameSystemSceneController::isReadyToStartScene (the load screen's nerve waits there for the scene's worker): it also asks the host that every pipeline registered so far is made (Pipelines::pending() for the set queued, the workers raised to normal priority while the game waits). The load screen keeps stepping as it does for the scene's own load. (2) A draw whose pipeline is still missing in play (a material registered after the load, a settings change) is skipped for that frame and its job moved to the front of the queue at normal priority, never built on the render thread; Vulkan with pipeline libraries keeps its quick link. A miss is a timeline event and counted (made by draws first stays 0 after a stage's first picture). title: (wrong behaviour, suspected) Android's restart starts the new activity in the `:game` process and kills that same process in the same UI-thread task.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed. GameActivity.restartGame (on the UI thread) calls startActivity(GameActivity, NEW_TASK|CLEAR_TASK) and then Process.killProcess(myPid) at once; startActivity only asks the system, which starts the new GameActivity in the process named :game, and that is the one being killed: whether the new one lands in the dying process or a fresh one depends on timing (P-099's CLEAR_TASK also drops the launcher). Design (the ProcessPhoenix pattern): the game asks the launcher's process (a small exported-false activity or service there, Intent with the restart kind) and ends its own process; the launcher's side waits for the old :game pid to be gone (ActivityManager.getRunningAppProcesses, or the pid file) and then starts GameActivity in the task it belongs to, without CLEAR_TASK (P-099). Proof: a tablet run through the harness that asks for the restart 20 times and reads 20 new pids, each start check passing.

note: Read 11-18: confirmed in code. Dynamic resolution (renderer_d3d12.cpp, once per scene picture) aims the scene pictures' GPU time at resolution_budget_ms(present_frame_rate(cap, VSync, refresh)), the display's rate; the interpolation governor (render_core.cpp interp_gpu_governor) picks k generated pictures a step from interpolation_gpu_cost_ms against 0.9 of a step and runs the slot clock at 60 x (k + 1). Neither reads the other: with k capped below the display's rate the pictures come at 60 x (k + 1) while dynamic resolution budgets 1/refresh, so it lowers the resolution further than the rate in use needs; the cheaper pictures then let the interpolation governor raise k after 2 s, which tightens the real budget again, a slow loop between the two (dynamic resolution steps up after 60 pictures, k after 120 sequences). Design: one controller owns both (k, sixteenths) against one budget, the slot period in use: the display's rate is filled first (k up to refresh/60 - 1) at no less than the resolution floor, then resolution rises in the time left; over budget, resolution falls to the floor before k falls. With in-between pictures on, a step's real picture is shown about two steps after the step, or never (I-002), so work is that arrival delay or 0 (the budget left as it was), and the phase aims at vblank - (delay + 1.5 ms), not at the step's own work. Design: the measure is keyed by the step: the render thread records, for each frame index, when that step's list was taken and its picture rendered (one slot per frame index, written beside the timeline's SubmitEnd and RenderSubmitted), and next_frame_start reads the entry of the step that started at previous_ns, with or without in-between pictures. Proof: a unit test of the measure fed a step rendered at +5 ms whose real picture is shown at +30 ms: work 5 ms (before: 30 ms or 0); and the timeline at 120 Hz with interpolation, StepWaitEnd against VBlank.
